runbook: R-18 / R-19 (independent oracle, blind to the change under test)

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.limitation: The export contains no scenario definition and no golden baseline (grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong' and 'coupled_scenarios' over data/ returns nothing). The scenario roster, levels, fight length and target resistances are therefore unknown, so the derivation below is a constrained reconstruction from the two published totals plus the cached wiki constants, not a full re-simulation.

sources_quoted.text: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.reading: {{rd|A|B}} is the wiki's melee/ranged split, melee value first. Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken if the Bloodsong wielder is melee, +5% if ranged. The amplifier is on the TARGET and applies to damage 'from all sources', i.e. to the whole roster's damage into that target while the 4 s debuff is up.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json — corroboration of the melee-first convention of {{rd|..|..}}
text: Ravenous Hydra / Cleave: 'Basic attacks on-hit deal {{as|{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}|ad}} physical damage to other enemies…' (Hydra cleave is 40% AD melee, 20% AD ranged)
Blade of the Ruined King / Mist's Edge: '…equal to {{as|{{rd|9%|6%}} of the target's current health}}' (9% melee, 6% ranged)
Death's Dance / Ignore Pain: 'Reduces {{rd|30%|10%}} of all post-mitigation physical and magic damage received…' (30% melee, 10% ranged)
sources_quoted.reading: Three items whose melee/ranged asymmetry is unambiguous all put the melee value first, so {{rd|8%|5%}} = 8% melee / 5% ranged, and never 5%/8%.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> 3877 Bloodsong -> buildsFrom [3867 'Bounty of Worlds'] and its Upgrade passive; item stats = {health 200, goldPer10 9} (no AD, no AH)
sources_quoted.text: 'You have completed the support quest and can now upgrade this item, Bounty of Worlds, for free into Bloodsong, Celestial Opposition, Dream Maker, Solstice Sleigh, or Zaz'Zak's Realmspike…'
sources_quoted.reading: Bloodsong is a support-quest upgrade; its holder in any roster scenario is the support slot, not the Black Cleaver carrier. Corroborated by data/worklists/e9-bis-b-task.md: 'Support starter upgrades withheld for ALL 173 champions: Bloodsong, Celestial Opposition, Dream Maker, Solstice Sleigh, Zaz'Zak's Realmspike'. The support-roster champions this repo exercises (data/champion-audit/batch-e9-3.json roster probes: Bard, Kayle, Milio, Nami, Sona, Yuumi; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json ally: Lulu) are all ranged, so the ranged branch (5%) is the one a roster scenario resolves.

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.reading: Current cache: 5 stacks x 6% = 30% max armor reduction (not the legacy 6 x 5%).

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 item 2 and the Section 5 audit table row 'Terminus/BC ramps'
sources_quoted.text: Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch)… the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes… Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean…
sources_quoted.reading: Used to test (and reject) Black Cleaver as the mechanism behind this leaf's delta — see alternatives_tested.

sources_quoted.text: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R) (apply_resistance, resistance.py); EHP round-trip raw = post*(1 + R/100)
sources_quoted.reading: The mitigation identity used in the Black Cleaver counter-check below.

independent_computation.step_2_candidate_constant: The only pair of numbers anywhere in the two named items' cached wiki text separated by exactly 3 percentage points is Bloodsong's Expose Weakness amplifier {{rd|8%|5%}} (S1). Black Cleaver's constants (6% per stack, 5 stacks, 30% cap, 6 s) contain no 3 pp pair (S4).
independent_computation.step_3_solve_the_amplified_subtotal: Model the leaf as incoming_damage = U + (1 + a) * S, where S is the post-mitigation damage taken inside the 4 s Expose Weakness window (amplified 'from all sources'), U is the unamplified remainder, and a is the amplifier. Then delta = (0.08 - 0.05) * S = 33.0  =>  S = 33.0 / 0.03 = 1100.0.
independent_computation.step_6_pick_the_branch: Bloodsong can only be held by the support-quest slot (S3), and every support this repo drives through its roster/ally path is ranged. The wiki's ranged value is 5% (S1, S2). A fix that introduces the melee/ranged branch changes ONLY the scenarios whose wielder is ranged — which is exactly the situation that produces a diff here — and in those scenarios 5% is the wiki-correct amplifier. Direction of the observed change (damage down) matches 8% -> 5%; the reverse fix would have raised the leaf.
independent_computation.conclusion: The wiki-correct value for a ranged Bloodsong wielder is 4041.9. The old 4074.9 is the value produced by using the melee (first) token of {{rd|8%|5%}} unconditionally — the 'index the first value' failure mode the repo's own rule 6 warns against.

alternatives_tested.hypothesis: Black Cleaver armor-reduction model changed (30% -> 24%, i.e. dropping to the 0.8*max_stacks average).
alternatives_tested.test: Treating the leaf as physical damage mitigated by 100/(100+A_eff) (S6): (100 + 0.70A) * (4074.9/4041.9) = 100 + 0.76A  =>  A = 15.0 armor.
alternatives_tested.outcome: Rejected — 15 armor is not a plausible target armor for a late-game roster scenario.

alternatives_tested.hypothesis: Black Cleaver constant replaced by the documented Cesaro mean (S5): 4.0 stacks (24%) -> 3.75 stacks (22.5%) at h = 8 hits.
alternatives_tested.outcome: Numerically possible (93 armor is realistic) but requires the ENTIRE 4 kilo-damage leaf to be physical with zero penetration, which a mixed roster fight is not; and it needs a free hit-count parameter. Weaker than the exact 3 pp Bloodsong fit, which needs no resistance assumption at all. Note this alternative also lands on new_value_correct, since it replaces a documented tuning constant with the exact Cesaro mean.

alternatives_tested.hypothesis: Expose Weakness was narrowed from 'all sources' to the wielder's own damage only (8% amp dropped from 412.5 of ally damage).
alternatives_tested.test: delta = 0.08 * S' => S' = 412.5; U' = 4074.9 - 1.08*412.5 = 3629.4. Arithmetically consistent.
alternatives_tested.outcome: Rejected on the wiki text: S1 says the debuff causes the target to 'take ... increased damage from all sources'. Narrowing it would be a regression, and only under this reading would the old value be correct. It is also implausible as a 0.8% effect — dropping the team-wide scope of a 4 s amp would move many more leaves, and by more.

caveats: The scenario definition is outside the permitted evidence tree, so the amplified subtotal S = 1100.0 and remainder U = 2886.9 are recovered from the two published totals rather than independently simulated. Both totals are reproduced exactly (to the published 0.1) by a single integer subtotal under the two wiki constants, which is the strength of the fit.

If the Bloodsong wielder in this roster is in fact melee, the melee branch (8%) and hence the OLD value would be correct. Nothing in the permitted evidence names the wielder; the ranged conclusion rests on Bloodsong being a support-quest-only item (S3) and on every support in this repo's roster/ally probes being ranged.
